    Deleting maximal cohooks from string endpoints #

    In Butler--Ringel's peak cases, the endpoint operation is not a new hook: the given word is already a maximal cohook extension of a shorter word, and the cohook is deleted. This file packages that relation in the direction used by right-module Auslander--Reiten sequences. Its canonical map goes from the shortened word into the original word and is therefore the existing negative-boundary inclusion.

    The left-hand construction is defined on reversed words but exposes maps and positions in the original orientation.
